issues.description: The template Lecture class defines addGuestStudents with signature addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, boolean validateInput) while the problem statement UML and the solution implement addGuestStudents(int). This parameter mismatch is structural: students following the template will implement or call a different method signature than specified in the exercise, causing confusion and preventing a direct match to the intended API.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the template with the UML and solution by changing the template method signature to public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents). If input validation is desired, implement it inside that method or provide an overloaded private/helper method (e.g. private void addGuestStudentsInternal(int, boolean)) or add a public overload addGuestStudents(int) that delegates to the two-parameter variant. Ensure the template's public API matches the problem statement.

issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify a method addGuestStudents(int) but the template Lecture.java declares addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, boolean validateInput), while the solution implements addGuestStudents(int). This signature mismatch (extra boolean parameter and different parameter list) creates a mapping confusion: students will follow the exercise description expecting a single-parameter method but the provided template uses a different method signature, which may prevent straightforward implementation or cause test mismatches.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the template method signature to match the problem statement and solution: declare public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents) (or provide an overload with that exact signature) so students can directly implement the requested method and align with the UML and reference solution.
